title: Kurt Schwitters, Mz 245. Mal Kah, 1921
lede: A small Merz collage built from cigarette packaging, a Bayer label, a ticket, and painted paper, with the brand names left as type.
summary: Cut cigarette labels with “MAL-KAH” and “BLUME”, a Bayer mark, and blue and brown papers. Kurt Schwitters, Hannover, 1921.

source.label: Lempertz, sale 877, lot 1062: Kurt Schwitters, Mz 245. Mal Kah. Merzzeichnung

evidence.note: Inspected the Commons image taken from the Lempertz auction catalogue ([Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kurt_Schwitters_Mz_245_Mal_Kah_Merzzeichnung.jpg), 3353 × 4250 px original, viewed at 1200 px). The Lempertz page itself was not opened. The current owner is not known.

styles.note: A Merz collage: found printed matter with its own type, cut edges, and paper tones. Partial fit: the commercial labels, not set type, carry the lettering, and there is no photograph.

context: Commons, after the Lempertz catalogue, describes the work as “Mz 245. Mal Kah. Merzzeichnung”: collage of colored and printed papers, card, and colored chalk on paper, 12.6 × 10 cm, mounted on card 23.4/23.8 × 18 cm, signed and dated K. Schwitters 1921, catalogue raisonné Orchard 83. [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kurt_Schwitters_Mz_245_Mal_Kah_Merzzeichnung.jpg).

Schwitters called his collages Merz, after a fragment of found text from the phrase “Commerz und Privatbank”. [Wikipedia: Kurt Schwitters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Schwitters). Compare his magazine [Merz 1](ref:schwitters-merz-1-holland-dada-1923) and the cover of [Anna Blume](ref:schwitters-anna-blume-dichtungen-1919).
observed: A cigarette label with “„MAL-KAH“” in black bold slab-serif capitals, framed by thin ornamental rules, fills the upper middle. A second “„MAL-KAH“” appears below it.
A strip with a circled monogram “J D Z” and “BLUME” in a plain heavy grotesque lies across the first label.
At the top a fragment reads “…urreine Zigarette” upside down.
At the left are a round “BAYER” cross mark on a label reading “SCHUTZ-MARKE”, a piece of checked paper, a black-grey wedge, and a strip of blue paper.
A patch of deep blue chalk covers part of a printed ticket or form with Fraktur text. Small cut pieces at the right show a black and pink letter and an ornamental print.

The pieces are mostly rectangles and triangles with straight cut edges. The colors are brown card, cream, black, and blue. The signature “Mz 245. Mal Kah” and “K. Schwitters 1921.” are in pencil on the mount.
interpretation: The collage shows how Dada makes type from printed waste: brand names, a trademark, and a ticket keep their own faces and are cut and layered at angles. The upside-down fragment and the clash of slab, grotesque, and Fraktur letters echo the typographic sheets.
borrow: Build a heading area from fragments of real labels, each keeping its own face, and overlap them at slight angles.
Use one strong blue patch as the only saturated color in a brown and cream field.

images.alt: Small collage of brown card, cigarette labels reading MAL-KAH and BLUME, a round Bayer trademark, checked paper, a black wedge, blue paper, and a patch of blue chalk, signed Mz 245 Mal Kah, K. Schwitters 1921 on the mount.
images.caption: Kurt Schwitters, *Mz 245. Mal Kah*, 1921, collage. Image from the Lempertz catalogue via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kurt_Schwitters_Mz_245_Mal_Kah_Merzzeichnung.jpg), PD-Art. The cigarette labels and the Bayer mark are anonymous commercial printing from before 1921.

rights.statement: Commons tags the image PD-Art (PD-old-auto-expired, death year 1948). Schwitters, a German author, died in 1948, so the collage is public domain in Germany. In the United States the collage is public domain whether or not it was published before 1931, because the life-plus-70 term for unpublished works ended in 2018. The pasted labels are anonymous commercial printing of about 1921 or earlier. The Bayer cross is still a trademark, which does not restrict this documentary use.
